title: Open-label phase I/II clinical trial of SARS-CoV-2 receptor binding domain-tetanus toxoid conjugate vaccine (FINLAY-FR-2) in combination with receptor binding domain-protein vaccine (FINLAY-FR-1A) in children.
ehr_evidence: Data were collected through physical examinations, parent interviews, and clinical laboratory assays (PCR, ELISA, neutralization titers, T-cell response) conducted as part of the clinical trial.
summary: Open-label phase I/II clinical trial evaluating the safety and immunogenicity of a heterologous SARS-CoV-2 vaccine regimen in children aged 3-18 years in Cuba.
key_findings: Local pain was the most common adverse event (47.7%), with no serious or severe vaccine-associated adverse events.
Two doses of FINLAY-FR-2 induced seroconversion in 96.2% (95% CI 93.5; 98.0) of participants.
The third heterologous dose increased seroconversion to 100% and anti-RBD IgG to 325.7 UA/ml.
Geometric mean neutralizing titers were 173.8 (95% CI 131.7; 229.5) vs Alpha, 142 (95% CI 101.3; 198.9) vs Delta, 24.8 (95% CI 16.8; 36.6) vs Beta, and 99.2 (95% CI 67.8; 145.4) vs Omicron.
Predicted clinical efficacy against D614G was 91.3% (95% CI 84.6; 95.1) after two doses and 97.4% (95% CI 91.5; 99.2) after three doses.
Immune response was non-inferior to young adults (cVNT50 GMT ratio 1.25, 95% CI 0.77; 2.02).
study_design: Open-label, adaptive, multicenter phase I/II clinical trial
population: Children and adolescents aged 3-18 years in Havana, Cuba
limitations: Lack of a placebo-controlled design due to ethical concerns
No concurrent reference population for immunobridging
Approximate comparison of viral neutralization titers between children and adults due to different sampling timepoints
